title: kithd: peer_fetch.rs — SSRF validator + TailnetCertVerifier extract
description:
Create crates/kithd/src/peer_fetch.rs with:
1. is_valid_fetch_host(host: &str) -> bool — SSRF-safe validator
2. TailnetCertVerifier extracted from discovery.rs (make it pub(crate) and import in both places)
3. build_tailnet_https_client() -> Client<_, Full<Bytes>> — shared client builder

What: factored-out network utilities for any kithd code that makes outbound HTTPS calls to tailnet peers.

Algorithm for is_valid_fetch_host:
1. Parse host (strip optional :port)
2. Reject if host is empty
3. Reject loopback: 127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost (case-insensitive)
4. Reject unspecified: 0.0.0.0, ::
5. Reject RFC1918: 10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x (parse as IP; if parsing fails it's a hostname, skip this check)
6. Reject link-local: 169.254.x.x, fe80::/10
7. Port (if present) must parse as u16 and be 1-65535
8. Accept all other values (MagicDNS hostnames, tailnet IPs 100.x.x.x)

Defensive programming:
- IP range checks use std::net::IpAddr::parse; never do string matching on IP prefixes
- Never log the host value at level above debug
- build_tailnet_https_client must call rustls::crypto::CryptoProvider::get_default() to avoid panic on missing provider

Tests (unit, no I/O):
- Oracle: known-bad inputs (loopback, RFC1918, link-local) and known-good inputs (100.x.x.x Tailscale IP, MagicDNS hostname, custom port); expected results from the validation rules above
- loopback rejected: 127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost
- RFC1918 rejected: 10.0.0.1, 172.16.0.1, 192.168.1.1
- link-local rejected: 169.254.1.1
- valid Tailscale IP accepted: 100.64.0.1
- valid MagicDNS hostname accepted: alice-kith.tail-xxxxx.ts.net
- custom port accepted: alice.ts.net:8443
- port 0 rejected
- invalid port (99999) rejected
